title: Choose the visual world for Central News
question: The roll assigned Transit Line. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Transit Line
options.lineage: metro wayfinding signage and line diagrams
options.thesis: Today's news drawn as a line: the lead story is the interchange, every headline after it is a stop with its time.
options.viewport: Red-roundel top bar, line-badge category row, the lead story on one red plate, then stops down a coloured line, each with its time in a fixed column.
options.risk: If the line is decorative rather than tied to time and category, it reads as a costume.

raised.raise: One reversed plate per screen: only the lead story sits on brand red; rank is carried by weight and reversal, not by more colour.
Times sit in one fixed, tight column beside every stop, read like a running order.
Density courage: stops pack edge to edge with no card containers; a saved story is marked on its own stop.
Structure comes from 1px hairlines and the line itself, never from card shadows.
Every stop's thumbnail shares one fixed size and baseline, so the column scans as a single register.
Hierarchy by scale contrast: the lead headline sits a full type step above every stop.

options.label: Broadcast Bulletin
options.lineage: television news graphics: lower-thirds, live bugs, tickers
options.thesis: The front page as the top-of-the-hour bulletin: one lead story in a lower-third, the rest as the running order.
options.viewport: Lead photo with a red lower-third headline bar and time bug, then a dense running order of headlines with source and time.
options.risk: The direction most news apps already borrow (red bars, 'live' bugs), so it reads familiar.

options.label: Type Specimen
options.thesis: Headlines as a live type specimen.
options.viewport: One giant headline with tiny labels.
options.case: Fuses poorly: commuters don't identify with a type foundry tool, and one giant glyph hides the day's ranking.
options.risk: A demo, not a news reader.

options.label: Timetable Slide Rack
options.thesis: Headlines as raked timetable slides at one type size.
options.viewport: A raked rack of slides read laterally.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the 11-degree rake and lateral travel fight one-handed vertical scanning.
options.risk: Ornament over task on a phone.
options.kept: One reversed plate per screen; rank by weight and reversal.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.thesis: A story tracked through stages on fixed-scale plates.
options.viewport: Five same-scale plates on one baseline.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a daily catch-up has no life-cycle to align, and cream plates are the category's spent default.
options.risk: Precious where the task is fast.
options.kept: Fixed scale and a shared baseline for every thumbnail.

options.label: Cassette J-Card
options.thesis: The day's headlines as a hand-ruled tracklist.
options.viewport: Side A and Side B tracklists with right-aligned times.
options.case: Fuses poorly: handwriting undermines the trust a news source needs.
options.kept: Times in one tight, fixed column.

options.label: Convention Catalog
options.thesis: Every story as a stamp-sized thumbnail in a packed grid.
options.viewport: Hundreds of tiny thumbnails packed edge to edge.
options.case: Fuses poorly: headlines need words, not stamp-sized drawings, to be judged.
options.kept: Density courage and marks on the item itself.

options.label: Design Annual Plates
options.thesis: Stories as registered plates with crosshairs and stamps.
options.viewport: A 4-up plate row with hairline credits.
options.case: Fuses poorly: gallery furniture slows a commuter's scan.
options.risk: Art-book pacing on a news feed.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The news-aggregator layout readers already know, executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Chip row, a large top story card, then image-left headline rows.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from Google News by design.
